subject: Mathematics
learning_goal: Master the chapter content using source-grounded explanations, practice and revision.

sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: PATTERNS IN MATHEMATICS 1 1.1 What is Mathematics?
sections.source_evidence: PATTERNS IN MATHEMATICS 1 1.1 What is Mathematics?

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: Mathematics is, in large part, the search for patterns, and for the explanations as to why those patterns exist.
sections.source_evidence: Mathematics is, in large part, the search for patterns, and for the explanations as to why those patterns exist.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: Such patterns indeed exist all around us — in nature, in our homes and schools, and in the motion of the sun, moon, and stars.
sections.source_evidence: Such patterns indeed exist all around us — in nature, in our homes and schools, and in the motion of the sun, moon, and stars.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: They occur in everything that we do and see, from shopping and cooking, to throwing a ball and playing games, to understanding weather patterns and using technology.
sections.source_evidence: They occur in everything that we do and see, from shopping and cooking, to throwing a ball and playing games, to understanding weather patterns and using technology.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: The search for patterns and their explanations can be a fun and creative endeavour.
sections.source_evidence: The search for patterns and their explanations can be a fun and creative endeavour.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: It is for this reason that mathematicians think of mathematics both as an art and as a science.
sections.source_evidence: It is for this reason that mathematicians think of mathematics both as an art and as a science.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: This year, we hope that you will get a chance to see the creativity and artistry involved in discovering and understanding mathematical patterns.
sections.source_evidence: This year, we hope that you will get a chance to see the creativity and artistry involved in discovering and understanding mathematical patterns.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: It is important to keep in mind that mathematics aims to not just find out what patterns exist, but also the explanations for why they exist.
sections.source_evidence: It is important to keep in mind that mathematics aims to not just find out what patterns exist, but also the explanations for why they exist.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: Such explanations can often then be used in applications well beyond the context in which they were discovered, which can then help to propel humanity forward.
sections.source_evidence: Such explanations can often then be used in applications well beyond the context in which they were discovered, which can then help to propel humanity forward.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: Ganita Prakash | Grade 6 2 For example, the understanding of patterns in the motion of stars, planets, and their satellites led humankind to develop the theory of gravitation, allowing us to launch our own satellites and send rockets to the Moon and to Mars; similarly, understanding patterns in genomes has helped in diagnosing and curing diseases — among thousands of other such examples.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: Can you think of other examples where mathematics helps us in our everyday lives?
sections.source_evidence: Can you think of other examples where mathematics helps us in our everyday lives?

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: How has mathematics helped propel humanity forward? (You might think of examples involving: carrying out scientific experiments; running our economy and democracy; building bridges, houses or other complex structures; making TVs, mobile phones, computers, bicycles, trains, cars, planes, calendars, clocks, etc.) 1.2 Patterns in Numbers Among the most basic patterns that occur in mathematics are patterns of numbers, particularly patterns of whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, ...

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: The branch of Mathematics that studies patterns in whole numbers is called number theory.
sections.source_evidence: The branch of Mathematics that studies patterns in whole numbers is called number theory.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: Number sequences are the most basic and among the most fascinating types of patterns that mathematicians study.
sections.source_evidence: Number sequences are the most basic and among the most fascinating types of patterns that mathematicians study.
